units.source_text: 我又独自回到了房子里，坐在自己房间的桌旁，一边看报，一边想象着遥远的东京的情景。

en.t: I went back into the house alone again, sat at the desk in my room, and while reading the newspaper, imagined what distant Tokyo must be like.

units.source_text: 我的想象集中在日本最大的城市在怎样的黑暗中，怎样运转着的画面上。

en.t: My imagination fixed itself on the image of Japan's largest city, wondering in what kind of darkness it continued to move.

units.source_text: 在那漆黑的，又不能不运转的令人焦躁不安的喧嚣城市中，我看到了犹如一盏灯火的先生的家。

en.t: In that pitch-black, restless, clamorous city that had no choice but to keep moving, I saw Sensei's house like a single lamp.

units.source_text: 那时我还没有意识到，自己将不由自主地被这盏灯火卷入那无声的旋涡之中；

en.t: At that time I did not yet realize that I would be drawn, against my will, by that lamp into a silent whirlpool;

units.source_text: 当然更没有意识到，自己面临的是，再过些时日，眼前的这盏灯火就会骤然消失的命运。

en.t: and of course I had still less realized that what lay before me was the fate of seeing that lamp vanish suddenly after a little more time had passed.

units.source_text: 我拿起笔，想把家乡发生的这件事写信告诉先生。

en.t: I picked up my pen, intending to write to Sensei and tell him about what had happened at home.

units.source_text: 可是，只写了十来行便又放下了笔。

en.t: But after writing only ten lines or so, I put the pen down again.

units.source_text: 我把信撕成碎片，扔进纸篓里。

en.t: I tore the letter into pieces and threw it into the wastebasket.

units.source_text: （因为我觉得给先生写这些东西也没用，根据上封信的经验，先生根本不会回信的。）

en.t: (Because I felt there was no point in writing such things to Sensei, and judging from my previous letter, he would not reply at all.)

units.source_text: 我太寂寞了，所以才会写信，并且盼望着先生能回信。

en.t: I was so lonely that I wrote the letter, and I longed for Sensei to send me a reply.
